research: https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/ultimate-prompting-guide-for-nano-banana — Google's own guide (Mar 2026): Subject + Action + Location + Composition + Style; name real cameras, lenses and film stocks; state angle and depth of field; describe what you want rather than negatives; 9:16 is supported natively; with references, say how the reference relates to the new scene.

https://fliki.ai/blog/nano-banana-2-prompting-guide — practitioner: Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image) does best with specific materials, light sources and camera position; generic style words give a generic look.
https://www.pixelbin.io/blog/nano-banana-prompt-guide — mood, materials, lighting, camera perspective and design style each need to be spelled out; clearly defined subject/action/context.

https://scas.nhs.uk/?p=35831 — UK crews do CPR in the back of moving ambulances; unrestrained crew at speed is a real safety risk (bracing, swaying bodies are authentic); LUCAS devices exist but manual compressions remain common, so manual is believable.

https://eprints.kingston.ac.uk/33844/12/Quinn-T-33844-VoR.pdf — PARAMEDIC trial (four UK services): resuscitation in a moving vehicle is hard, competing tasks (defib, airway, bagging) happen at once: one compresses, one manages airway/monitor.

https://britishcinematographer.co.uk/?p=109268 — UK drama lit an ambulance interior 360 degrees with diffused LED tubes replacing fluorescents, swinging lights outside to fake passing streetlamps and siren glow; aim was cold and sickly but with readable skin.

https://www.newsshooter.com/2026/09/15/capturing-chaos-inside-the-camera-lighting-workflow-of-hbos-the-pitt/ — The Pitt hides light in the set's practicals and keeps a continuous, live-feeling camera; emergency scenes read as real because light comes from fixtures in shot.

https://www.buzzfeed.com/arianelange/criminal-minds-hashtag-its-light-bulbs — TV crews put blue gels on ambulance windows because outside light read too orange; night in a vehicle should read blue-cold with real light sources ('you need light to make dark').
attach_reference: yes — attach it as a layout and set reference only (white cupboards, teal seats, black strapped mattress, hatch to the cab): it anchors a real UK interior better than words, but the photo is empty, daylit and calm, so each prompt still states night, rain, hard strip light, monitor glow and blue strobe, and tells the model to keep the layout but relight it.
notes: Sell the speed in the edit: a small handheld shake, a few frames of blue flash timed to the siren, and the shouted 'BP 60 over 30, we're gonna lose him!' over the cut. Keep the monitor numbers unreadable in the still and add a real trace or numbers in post only if wanted. If attaching the reference, say in the box: 'Use the attached photo for the ambulance interior layout only; relight it as described.'

prompts.idea: Wide from the rear doors: the whole fight in one frame, down the stretcher to the hatch and the driver's back; geography first, matches the reference angle.
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 handheld frame from the rear doors of a UK ambulance at night, looking forward down the length of the black stretcher toward the small hatch window and the driver's back. A male paramedic in a plain dark-green uniform, blue gloves and surgical mask kneels over a grey-skinned older man in an oxygen mask, locked arms mid-compression. A female paramedic braced against white cupboards and a teal seat points at a heart monitor glowing green with a ragged trace, shouting behind her mask. Hard cold ceiling strip light, blue emergency light strobing through the hatch, rain streaks on the cab windscreen. Shot on 35mm Kodak Vision3 500T, slight motion blur from the swaying vehicle, heavy grain, slightly underexposed. Thanks.

prompts.idea: Monitor in the foreground, low and tight: the green ragged trace fills the bottom of the frame, the shouting paramedic's masked face sharp behind it; the dying is told by the machine.
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 tight close shot inside a speeding UK ambulance at night, camera low beside a portable heart monitor bolted to a white cupboard. In the soft foreground the monitor screen glows green with a fast, jagged, chaotic heart trace and blurred unreadable numbers. Behind it, in sharp focus, a female paramedic in a plain dark-green uniform and surgical mask stares at the screen, eyes wide, sweat on her brow, mid-shout, one blue-gloved hand gripping a grab rail. Past her shoulder a male paramedic pumps a bag-valve mask over an older man's face. Cold fluorescent top light, green monitor glow on her skin, a slash of blue strobe across the teal seat. 50mm lens, shallow depth of field, 35mm film grain, handheld. Thanks.

prompts.idea: High overhead from the ceiling corner: compressions seen from above, kit and straps flying, the patient's grey face at the centre; reads as chaos and a body in trouble in one second.
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 steep high angle from the ceiling corner of a UK ambulance racing through rainy night streets, looking down on an older man lying on a black stretcher mattress, his grey face under an oxygen mask, shirt cut open, defibrillator pads on his chest, straps loose. A male paramedic in a plain dark-green uniform, blue gloves and surgical mask drives both hands into his chest, arms blurred with motion. A female paramedic, also masked, braces against the swaying wall, squeezing a bag-valve mask with one hand and holding a monitor lead in the other. Dropped gauze wrappers and tubing slide across the teal-green floor. Hard cold strip light from above, blue emergency light flaring through a side window, 24mm lens, 35mm film grain, underexposed, camera shake. Thanks.
